hook_text: A tyre stall, a tomato farm, a brick factory and a platinum mine share one river. Which of them will the town still have in thirty years?
clip_script: In one Limpopo town, a sole trader fixes tyres with two young assistants: small, but real jobs close to home. Two brothers farm tomatoes as partners, twelve workers all year and thirty at harvest. A private brick company gives sixty steady jobs. A public mining company employs three thousand and buys from local suppliers. Every one of them uses the valley: water, soil, clay, rock. Drip irrigation, cleaner kilns, recycled tyres and repaired mine land keep the valley alive. The test of a good business is three things, not one: people, planet and profit.
visual_style: A whiteboard river valley with four businesses along the bank, worker icons multiplying, a water level line, and three stacked words: people, planet, profit.
mood: Hopeful but honest, a town's future in the balance.
pacing: A wide opening shot, four quick portraits, a slower turn to the river, and a firm three-word close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and judge each business by people, planet and profit.
